newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita first quarter neutral - analysts.
newsitem.headline: Merita first quarter neutral - analysts.

text.p: Finnish bank Merita Oy's sharply higher than expected rise in first quarter earnings included surprisingly high gains from share disposals, but the overall signals were neutral, analysts said on Wednesday.

Merita reported operating profit after credit losses at 934 million markka, up from 233 million in the year-ago period, boosted by a 584 million markka gain from the systematic downsizing of the group equity portfolio by 2.6 billion markka to 4.3 billion.
Analysts' median forecast in a Reuters poll had been for a 431 million markka first quarter operating profit.
After the release of the Q1 report, analysts said their earlier consensus for the full-year -- the median had been a 1.85 billion operating profit -- would probably rise.

"I think that based on this, consensus estimates for the full-year will rise somewhat," said Risto Murto, analyst at Erik Selin, noting that Merita had said the 584 million markka gain was non-recurring and would not change the long-term business outlook.
In 1996, Merita posted a 1.2 billion markka operating profit after credit losses.
"My view is that the better-than-expected profit will give a short-term positive share reaction, which is also supported by overall stock market sentiment," Murto said.

The size of disposals was a surprise but the fact that the bulk of what Merita had sold was blue chips, and bourse volumes were at a record high early this year, explained how the bank could sell such a massive slice virtually unnoticed, analysts said.

Evli analyst Christian Kock said the first quarter report was neutral news all in all, with the higher-than-expected share disposal gain and a strong performance in credit losses which points to an annual rate of one percent on one hand, but squeezed margins in core banking operations on the other.
"Looking at core banking, it does not look very beautiful, there is tough competition for clients," he said.
FIM Securities analyst Niklas Geust said there had been little improvement in the core banking business.

"So far, the core banking business net of securities sales, dividends and credit losses has remained stable for the past six quarters -- or, in other words, there has hardly been any improvement at all," Geust said.

Merita has earlier said it expected operating profit to improve on last year, but now said it expected clearly better net earnings, which it said was in fact a more positive statement than its previous forecast.

It repeated that credit losses and costs would continue to fall, and most of the synergy benefits from the merger of Unitas and Kansallis-Osake-Pankki, which created the group in 1995, would be felt this year.
Merita shares rose 0.50 markka or almost three percent to 18.50 markka after the announcement but eased to 18.30 markka by noon.
